name: A01-greeting-heard-once
notes:
The bug this case exists for is PR #224: the begin message spoken twice, the second copy starting before the first had finished. It is invisible to every other layer — the platform logs one greeting, because it only ever generated one — and it is the first thing a real listener hears. The mood answer that follows keeps the call on the ordinary path so the greeting is graded in the context it ships in, not in isolation. `no_duplicate_utterance` is what catches the doubling; the expectations here only pin down that this was the right call at all. Line 2 answers the sleep question the mood phase asks BEFORE moving on to the medication: a scripted caller that ignores a question leaves the phase open, `log_mood` never fires, and the case fails on its own rigidity rather than on the prompt — which is what the first run of it did.

The two `times: 1` assertions are here because of what the Live model did on this exact case: it logged the mood, the dose and the outcome TWICE each, a turn having been abandoned after its tools ran and then regenerated. A bare `tool_called` reads that as a clean call, and downstream it is a duplicated row in somebody's record.

tools.recall_lead_context: {"summary_text": "Margaret, CA, trial day 3 of 7. Mood last 3 days: 4,4,3. Today's meds: Lipitor at 08:00, Metformin at 19:00."}

script: I'm doing alright, thank you Clara.
